title: New detections of Galactic molecular absorption systems toward ALMA calibrator sources
question: Do ALMA calibrator spectra in the archive contain Galactic molecular absorption lines, and what do HCO/H13CO+ ratios imply about the diffuse ISM?

what.value: HCO and H13CO+ column densities toward previous HCO-absorption sightlines

evidence.quote: compared with the values measured on the lines-of-sight of the sources toward which HCO absorption was previously detected ((cite: Liszt+14))
along with the values in several PDRs ((cite: Schilke+01); (cite: Gerin+09))

recipe.method: Select 36 archive calibrators by Cycle 0 availability, >0.2 Jy continuum, <1 MHz resolution FDM
CLEAN cubes from calibrated visibilities; flag and interpolate absorbing bandpass channels, reapply bandpass
Continuum subtraction, divide by continuum, Gaussian fit for velocity, FWHM, depth

recipe.goal: derive optical depths and column densities
recipe.method: tau from line/continuum ratio; N from Greaves & Nyman formula with Gaussian integrated tau
Compare ratios with literature PDR and diffuse sightline values

evidence.quote: the $T_{\mathrm{ex}}$ of the main CO component is calculated to be 6.2 K

answer_key.quantity: CO total column density J1604-446 main component

evidence.quote: the total column density and $T_{\mathrm{ex}}$ of the main CO component are determined to be $1.1 \times 10^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ and 6.2 K

not_stated_but_needed: Image size, cell size, channel width and velocity resolution of cubes
Which spectral windows/EBs per source and CASA version
Beam size / extraction aperture for spectra
Fitting method for Gaussians and error budget details
missing_for_reproduction: Spectral window and execution block lists
score_reason: Public data and simple analysis, but imaging details and CASA version missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, simple recipe, numeric ratios.
